answer: Per-task micro-royalty thread. Each identity accrues rewards only along a verified action thread: every new action must cite prior outputs and inherit their reputation weight. Cloning resets weight to zero, so clones must rebuild a full citation history before earning. The marginal clone costs real compute and time to re-derive each ancestor link, while paying full protocol nectar for submissions that yield near-zero weight. Attackers thus subsidize the network with wasted work; each additional clone worsens returns, and the nebula of duplicate threads is throttled by citation quotas.
